statement: A lantern renews what the dark would unwrite; carry one into every vault.
detail: Light is memory made visible. Where the lantern-glow falls, the Fade loosens its grip and forgotten things take shape again.

source_ref.quote: Carry a lantern, and the dark forgets to swallow you.

statement: Name a thing three times and it stays; name it once and the moss takes it back.
detail: Recall is a rope thrown across the Fade. One throw frays; three throws hold. The Keepers count under their breath for a reason.

source_ref.quote: Once is a guess, twice is a hope, thrice is a knot the moss cannot loosen.

statement: The swollen books remember more than they show — read the margins, not the middle.
detail: In the Sunken Reading-Room the truest notes are the ones scrawled sideways by frightened hands. The printed page is only what someone wanted kept.

source_ref.quote: What a book fears to say aloud, it whispers in its margins.

statement: A ward opens only to the prepared: answer its riddle from memory, or the door stays stone.
detail: The old wards do not bargain and do not wait. They test what you carry in your head, not what you carry in your pack.

source_ref.quote: The door asked, and I had no answer, and so the door remained a wall.

statement: The Moss-Warden grew around a stolen truth and will trade it back only to one who already half-knows it.
detail: It is less a monster than a knot: a great mossy sentinel wound tight about a single fact the Fade tried to eat. Loosen the knot with recall and the truth spills free.

source_ref.quote: It hoards one truth the way a dragon hoards gold, and guards it just as jealously.
